sources.title: LCD Keypad & LCD Proximity Keypad — RP432KP / RP432KPP
sources.edition: 5IN1425 H · PDF metadata created January 2022 · six-page English extract
sources.publisher: RISCO Group (original manufacturer document; Maxwell mirror)
sources.pageNumbering: The available PDF is the six-page English portion. Printed page equals one-based PDF page; control instructions pp3–6.
sources.scope: Physical RP432KP / RP432KPP control functions. Other keypad styles remain separate. Revision H is identified in PDF title/metadata; the multilingual remainder is not included in this download.

baseline: Installer 5IN2048 G (06/2020); separately labelled UK user 5IN2124 E (08/2021); physical keypad 5IN1425 H (01/2022). No LightSYS+ or latest-firmware equivalence.

gaps.reason: Installer G (2020) and UK user E (2021) are distinct documented baselines. UK Set/Omit/Fault terminology is not silently substituted for installer Arm/Bypass/Trouble.
gaps.question: Which installed LightSYS2 firmware/language should the combined experience target?
gaps.neededEvidence: A version-screen photo and matching installer/user manual edition, with credentials redacted.

gaps.reason: Appendix p255 repeats Abort Alarm and its old type summary on p104 conflicts with the complete pp107–114 type table. p257 repeats PSTN Parameters as 2; detailed p153 verifies 3. Detailed pages take precedence.
gaps.question: Does the real target keypad match the detailed G tables for PSTN Parameters and zone types?
gaps.neededEvidence: Screen-by-screen capture of the affected local lists with firmware/version visible separately.

gaps.reason: Installed BUS/wireless detector and peripheral variants alter available fields. Reference branches expose the documented names without inventing extra model-selection menus or device responses.
gaps.question: Which BUS/wireless detector, sounder and keypad variants should gain working field wizards?
gaps.neededEvidence: Exact device model IDs and authorised recordings of their parameter and acknowledgement screens.

gaps.reason: Source p102 requires completing the entire One By One wizard to save. That wizard remains reference-only; confirmed By Category edits are functional.
gaps.question: At which exact screen does One By One record its entire zone edit, and how does cancellation behave?
gaps.neededEvidence: An authorised recording of a full zone wizard and a cancelled edit on the selected firmware.

gaps.reason: Source p102 says 15 characters for One By One, while p103 gives 16 for By Category. The functional By Category editor uses its own 16-character limit.
gaps.question: Does the target firmware accept 15 or 16 characters in each of the two zone-label methods?
gaps.neededEvidence: A non-sensitive test label entered through both One By One and By Category.

gaps.reason: Trigger selection is followed by conditional source, pattern, duration, logic and label steps. This programming wizard remains reference-only rather than pretending a single field completes it; separate operational output tests work.
gaps.question: Which conditional pattern/source/ALL–ANY screens appear for each output trigger family?
gaps.neededEvidence: An authorised recording of the complete output wizard with a safely isolated test output.

gaps.reason: The complete UK user function table gives order but no numerical quick-key addresses. User and service sessions use scrolling; no shortcut numbers are guessed.
gaps.question: What exact user/service menu order and local numbers are displayed on the UK target firmware?
gaps.neededEvidence: Pictures or video of every top-level user/service option after authorised entry; no authentication codes.

gaps.reason: All data are fictional local state. No codes, tag enrolment, RF exchanges, remote software, cloud registration, monitoring, reset algorithm or factory authentication is supplied.
gaps.question: Which disconnected service workflows are useful to model next?
gaps.neededEvidence: Manufacturer instructions and a bench-only screen sequence, excluding credentials and live monitoring actions.

gaps.reason: Detailed p214 prints 07.1 for both Lamp Type and Brightness, while appendix p261 prints 07.2 for Brightness. The conflicting Brightness quick code is not exposed as an interactive shortcut.
gaps.question: Is Lamp Brightness 07.1 or 07.2 on the specified BUS sounder and panel revision?
gaps.neededEvidence: The displayed Lamp submenu with the exact sounder model and firmware identified.

sourceCorrections.Zone types: Full table pp107–114 supersedes inconsistent old summary p104.
sourceCorrections.Device controls: p95–96 includes 4,6,7,8,9 omitted from appendix p254; no code 5 is invented.
sourceCorrections.Resistance: 2.1.3 p130 is configuration; diagnostic is installer Maintenance, p222.
sourceCorrections.Firmware: No specific firmware build asserted for the G manual; modern 5IN2912/LightSYS+ excluded.

fixtureValues: All stored values, records, event times, readings and device responses are fictional.
